<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="Sp1nd01" />{{rh|Reward of fooles.|Chap.ij.iij.|Wiſedomes fruits.}}</noinclude>you, I will make knowen my wordes vnto you.

{{Verse|1|24}} ¶ *{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text-align=left|text=* Iſa.65.12. and 66.4. ier.7.13. ezech.8.18}} Becauſe I haue called, and yee refuſed, I haue ſtretched out my hand, and no man regarded:

{{Verse|1|25}} But ye haue ſet at nought all my counſell, ⁊ would none of my reproofe:

{{Verse|1|26}} I alſo will laugh at your calamitie, I wil mocke when your feare commeth.

{{Verse|1|27}} *{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text-align=left|text=* Iob.27.9. iſa.1.15. ier.11.11. & 14.12.}} When your feare commeth as deſolation, and your deſtruction commeth as a whirlewinde; when diſtreſſe and anguiſh commeth vpon you:

{{Verse|1|28}} *{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text-align=left|text=* Micah.3.4}} Then ſhall they call vpon mee, but I will not anſwere; they ſhall ſeeke me early, but they ſhall not finde me:

{{Verse|1|29}} For that they hated knowledge, and did not chooſe the feare of the {{sc|Lord}}. 

{{Verse|1|30}} They would none of my counſel: they deſpiſed all my reproofe.

{{Verse|1|31}} Therefore ſhall they eate of the fruite of their owne way, and be filled with their owne deuices.

{{Verse|1|32}} For the ǁ{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text-align=left|text=ǁ'' Or, eaſe of the ſimple.''}} turning away of the ſimple ſhall ſlay them, and the proſperity of fooles ſhall deſtroy them.

{{Verse|1|33}} But who ſo hearkneth vnto mee, ſhall dwell ſafely, and ſhall be quiet from feare of euil.

==={{Chapter|2|CHAP. II.}}===
{{smaller block|[[#2:1|1]] Wiſedome promiſeth godlineſſe to her children, [[#2:10|10]] and ſafety from euill company, [[#2:20|20]] and direction in good wayes.}}

{{Verse|2|1|notext=}} 
{{dropinitial|M|image=King James Bible (1611) page D3v (M).png|imgsize=100px}}Y ſonne, if thou wilt receiue my words, and hide my commaundements with thee;

{{Verse|2|2}} So that thou incline thine eare unto wiſedome, {{smaller|and}} apply thine heart to vnderſtanding:

{{Verse|2|3}} Yea if thou cryeſt after knowledge, {{smaller|and}} †{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text-align=left|text=† ''Heb. giueſt thy voice''}} lifteſt vp thy voyce for vnderſtanding:

{{Verse|2|4}} *{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text-align=left|text=* Mat.13.44.}} If thou ſeekeſt her as ſiluer, and ſearcheſt for her, as {{smaller|for}} hid treaſures:

{{Verse|2|5}} Then ſhalt thou vnderſtand the feare of the {{sc|Lord}}, and find the knowledge of God.

{{Verse|2|6}} *{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text-align=left|text=* Iam.1.5. 1.king.3.9.}} For the {{sc|Lord}} giueth wiſedome: out of his mouth {{smaller|commeth}} knowledge, and vnderſtanding.

{{Verse|2|7}} He layeth vp ſound wiſedome for the righteous: {{smaller|he is}} a buckler to them that walke vprightly.

{{Verse|2|8}} He keepeth the pathes of iudgement, and preſerueth the way of his Saints.

{{Verse|2|9}} Then ſhalt thou vnderſtand righteouſneſſe, and iudgement, and equity; {{smaller|yea}} euery good path.

{{Verse|2|10}} ¶ When wiſedome entreth into thine heart, and knowledge is pleaſant vnto thy ſoule;

{{Verse|2|11}} Diſcretion ſhall preſerue thee, vnderſtanding ſhall keepe thee: 

{{Verse|2|12}} To deliuer thee from the way of the euill {{smaller|man}}, from the man that ſpeaketh froward things.

{{Verse|2|13}} Who leaue the pathes of vprightneſſe, to walke in the wayes of darkeneſſe:

{{Verse|2|14}} Who reioyce to doe euill, {{smaller|and}} delight in the frowardneſſe of the wicked.

{{Verse|2|15}} Whoſe wayes {{smaller|are}} crooked, and {{smaller|they}} froward in their pathes.

{{Verse|2|16}} To deliuer thee from the ſtrange woman, *{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text-align=left|text=* Prou. 5.3. and 7.5.}} {{smaller|euen}} from the ſtranger, {{smaller|which}} flattereth with her words:

{{Verse|2|17}} Which forſaketh the guide of her youth, and forgetteth the couenant of her God.

{{Verse|2|18}} For her houſe inclineth vnto death, and her pathes vnto the dead:

{{Verse|2|19}} None that goe vnto her, returne againe, neither take they hold of the pathes of life.

{{Verse|2|20}} That thou mayeſt walke in the way of good {{smaller|men}}, and keepe the pathes of the righteous.

{{Verse|2|21}} *{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text-align=left|text=* Pſal.37.30.}} For the vpright ſhall dewll in the land, and the perfect ſhall remaine in it.

{{Verse|2|22}} *{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text-align=left|text=* Iob.18.17. pſal.104.35.}} But the wicked ſhall be cut off from the earth, and the tranſgreſſours ſhalbe ǁ{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text-align=left|text=ǁ ''Or, pluckt vp.''}} rooted out of it.

==={{Chapter|3|CHAP. III.}}===
{{smaller block|[[#3:1|1]] An exhortation to obedience, [[#3:5|5]] to faith, [[#3:7|7]] to mortification, [[#3:9|9]] to deuotion, [[#3:11|11]] to patience. [[#3:13|13]] The happy gaine of wiſedome. [[#3:19|19]] The power, [[#3:21|21]] and the benefits of wiſedome. [[#3:27|27]] An exhortation to charitableneſſe, [[#3:30|30]] peaceableneſſe, [[#3:31|31]] and contentedneſſe. [[#3:33|33]] The curſed ſtate of the wicked.}}

{{Verse|1|1|notext=}}{{dropinitial|M|image=King James Bible (1611) page D4v (M).xcf|imgsize=100px}}Y ſonne, forget not my lawe; *{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text-align=left|text=* Deut.8.1. & 30.16.}} but let thine heart keepe my commaundements:

{{Verse|1|2}} For length of dayes, and †{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text-align=left|text=† ''Heb. yeeres of life.''}} long life, and peace ſhall they adde to thee.
